title: Front-End Only Validation
pattern: Performing validation/authorization checks only at the entry gateway (such as a front-end form or web client) and assuming inputs to the internal API are secure.
why_bad: An attacker can easily bypass the front-end client and send arbitrary HTTP payloads directly to the backend API, modifying other users' resources without authorization [30:235].
detection: Administrative or state-mutating endpoints that execute actions on resources using untrusted arguments without verifying the authenticated caller's permissions to modify that specific resource [30:235].
fix: Validate authentication, authorization, and structural constraints on every backend endpoint, regardless of upstream client checks [30:235].
source: *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (Adkins), Chapter 5; *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (Vernon), Chapter 14 [30:235].
